seen.extent: All 102 images viewed as contact sheets; images 039, 040 (both pages), 059, 068, 022, 023 and the key pages 100-101 at full size; 34 letter images screened half by half; images 043, 050 and 086 (a seeded random sample) read by a second, uninformed reader. About 25 letter images (039-059, 067-068, 080-081, 085-088) are the ones the earlier vetting took for a symbol script.
seen.cipher: None in the letters. The supposed symbol script is the ordinary German Kurrent hand of Landgravine Elisabeth Dorothea of Hessen-Darmstadt writing to Princess Dorothea Charlotte (Darmstadt 1687, Butzbach 1693-1698), about half of it photographed upside down and all of it with heavy show-through. Images 100-101 are a separate key: a reciprocal alphabet of 12 letter pairs written in roman letters, number signs, and a cover-name table for 15 persons and 5 places of the Württemberg court. No letter in the file has letter groups of that kind or any name from the table.

1637.closed: A key with no ciphertext: the letters of the file are in clear German Kurrent (pre-set test on letter 040: 164 of 222 and 174 of 224 transcribed words are dictionary words, the shortfall being illegible words; 0 of 6 odd words decode with the key; a blind second reader judged 3 of 3 randomly drawn letter images alphabetic German with no cipher). The key (images 100-101) is a Württemberg court code of about 1697-98 (inferred) whose use is not shown here. First reported by WAINUT, 3 Nov 2026.
1637.supersedes: The block of 2 Nov 2026 (verdict open) took the letters for a 'continuous symbol script' from contact sheets. At full size and turned the right way up they are clear German Kurrent; the key's worked examples are roman letter groups that occur in no letter. Same finding as WAINUT's note of 3 Nov 2026.
